message.content:
The “best” film of 2020 depends on what you’re looking for—critical acclaim, box‑office success, or cultural impact—but here are a few titles that stood out that year:

| Film | Why it mattered in 2020 |
|------|------------------------|
| **“The Trial of the Chicago 7”** | A gripping courtroom drama that earned widespread praise for its direction, ensemble cast, and timely political themes. It was a top pick for many critics and won several awards. |
| **“Soul”** | Pixar’s animated feature about life, purpose, and jazz music received universal acclaim for its storytelling, visuals, and soundtrack. It won the Academy Award for Best Animated Feature. |
| **“Tenet”** | Christopher Nolan’s mind‑bending action thriller pushed the limits of streaming releases and became a cultural talking point, especially given its release during the pandemic. |
| **“Nomadland”** | Though released in late 2019, it dominated the 2020 awards season, winning Best Picture at the Oscars and resonating with audiences for its quiet, contemplative look at modern American nomads. |
| **“Mank”** | David Fincher’s biopic about screenwriter Herman J. Mankiewicz was praised for its period detail and performances, earning an Oscar nomination for Best Picture. |

If you’re looking for a definitive “best” in terms of awards, **“Nomadland”** won Best Picture at the 2020 Oscars, making it the most celebrated film of that year. If you prefer a mix of critical praise and cultural relevance, **“The Trial of the Chicago 7”** and **“Soul”** are excellent choices.
